# SOP-P2-L2-01 Line startup - Ring Rolling line

Revision: Rev B  
Plant: P2, line P2-L2  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L2-IH01, EQ-P2-L2-HT02, EQ-P2-L2-RR03

Purpose
1. Define required actions and checks to bring the Ring Rolling line to production-ready status for safe, repeatable operation of EQ-P2-L2-IH01 (induction heater), EQ-P2-L2-HT02 (heat treat furnace), and EQ-P2-L2-RR03 (radial ring rolling mill).

Scope
2. Applies to operators, maintenance staff, and shift leads responsible for startup and initial production on P2-L2. See ECN-2026-050 for recent electrical changes, QS-PROC-07 for quality hold procedures, and SOP-P2-L2-05 for shutdown.

Background and rationale
3. Consistent startup sequencing prevents thermal shock to the furnace and avoids machine damage during ring transfer and rolling. EQ-P2-L2-HT02 must attain and stabilize at its process setpoint before ring loading to ensure metallurgical consistency; the austenitizing setpoint for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L2-HT02) is 855 °C. Lubrication for the rolling mill is critical to tool life and surface finish; the lubricant part number for Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #3 (EQ-P2-L2-RR03) is CFW-LUB-101. Records collected during startup form the basis for quality release and failure investigation.

Preconditions (must be satisfied before initiating startup)
4. a) Facility electrical mains and local disconnects for P2-L2 are verified closed and tagged per ECN-2026-050.  
b) Maintenance clearance completed and signed for any work on EQ-P2-L2-IH01, EQ-P2-L2-HT02, or EQ-P2-L2-RR03.  
c) All safety interlocks and emergency stops are present and tested.  
d) Material to be processed is staged and identified per part routing and QS-PROC-07.

Required PPE
5. a) Standard plant PPE: safety glasses, hearing protection, steel-toe footwear.  
b) Heat-resistant gloves and face shield for furnace handling.  
c) Arc-rated protective clothing if performing live electrical verification.  
d) Welding respirator when performing any brazing or torch operations associated with tooling changeover.

Startup procedure (numbered sequence)
6. 1) Pre-start visual inspection: Walk the line and inspect guards, conveyors, and overhead hoists for obstructions. Verify control cabinet doors are closed and sealed. Note any discrepancies in the startup log. Rationale: catching physical issues prevents electrical or mechanical damage upon energizing.

7. 2) Power application: With approvals in place, apply main power to line controls and local control panels. Verify control annunciators and PLC health indicators are normal. Rationale: establishing control power first ensures safe operator interaction.

8. 3) Induction heater warm-up: Enable EQ-P2-L2-IH01 per normal procedure and monitor for abnormal sounds or error codes. Confirm heater ready status on the HMI before proceeding. Record heater status in the startup log. Example entry: "IH01 ready; no faults."

9. 4) Furnace ramp and setpoint confirmation: Bring EQ-P2-L2-HT02 to process temperature and allow stabilization. The austenitizing setpoint for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L2-HT02) is 855 °C. Confirm control shows stable temperature and that alarm thresholds are enabled. Record actual furnace readback and time of stabilization in the startup log. Rationale: metallurgical consistency requires correct austenitizing conditions prior to ring rolling.

10. 5) Tooling and lubrication verification for rolling mill: Inspect RR03 tooling clearance and install rolling dies per tooling drawing. Apply lubricant CFW-LUB-101 to specified lubrication points and confirm delivery at the bearing and die manifolds. Log lubricant part number and quantity dispensed. Rationale: correct lubricant and application prevent surface defects and mechanical seizure.

11. 6) Dry run without charge: With the line clear, execute single-cycle test runs of transfer mechanisms and the rolling mill without workpieces. Observe sequence timing, transfer alignment, and interlock function. Record any deviations and corrective actions. Rationale: verifies motion profiles and safety interlocks under controlled conditions.

12. 7) Trial charge and quality verification: Process a qualified trial ring using established lot/sample procedures. Inspect dimensional and surface attributes per QS-PROC-07 sampling criteria. Place trial results in the process record and hold per QS-PROC-07 until quality sign-off. Rationale: ensures process outputs meet quality requirements before full production.

13. 8) Transition to production: After successful trial and quality approval, notify operations scheduling and begin normal production. Maintain continuous monitoring for the first production shift and record any out-of-spec events. Rationale: early detection of drift prevents large-scale rework.

Examples of acceptable records to retain
14. - Startup log entries including operator name, equipment status, and stabilization confirmation.  
- Furnace temperature stabilization entry showing setpoint and readback.  
- Lubrication log entry recording CFW-LUB-101 usage and dispensing location.  
- Trial ring inspection report and disposition per QS-PROC-07.  
- Any maintenance tags removed and associated clearance forms referenced per ECN-2026-050.

Non-conformance handling
15. If any step fails (interlock trips, furnace fails to stabilize at the austenitizing setpoint, abnormal vibrations), stop the startup sequence, lock out equipment, and initiate maintenance per SOP-P2-L2-05. Document the event and hold affected material per QS-PROC-07 until disposition.

Sign-off
16. Final acceptance of startup sequence requires signatures from the operating technician, maintenance lead, and shift supervisor. Records to be attached: startup log, furnace readback entry, lubrication entry with CFW-LUB-101 noted, and trial inspection form.

Revision notes and related documents
17. See ECN-2026-050 for electrical updates that affect energization sequence. Refer to QS-PROC-07 for quality hold and sample disposition. Use SOP-P2-L2-05 for shutdown and lockout/tagout procedures.

Approval
18. Operator print name and signature: __________________________  
Maintenance lead print name and signature: __________________________  
Shift supervisor print name and signature: __________________________

Controlled document: retain startup records in the document control system per plant retention policy.
